entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9248"/><div sID="gen15800" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9248"/><hi type="bold">8. heardest not--</hi>repeated, as also "knewest not," from <reference osisRef="Isa.48.7">Is 48:7</reference>.<div eID="gen15800" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15801" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from that time--</hi>Omit "that." "Yea, from the first thine ear did not open itself," namely, to obey them [Rosenmuller]. "To open the ear" denotes obedient attention (<reference osisRef="Isa.50.5">Is 50:5</reference>); or, "was not opened" to receive them; that is, they were not declared by Me to thee previously, since, if thou hadst been informed of them, such is thy perversity, thou couldst not have been kept in check [Maurer]. In the former view, the sense of the words following is, "For I knew that, if I had not foretold the destruction of Babylon so plainly that there could be no perverting of it, thou wouldst have perversely ascribed it to idols, or something else than to Me" (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.5">Is 48:5</reference>). Thus they would have relapsed into idolatry, to cure them of which the Babylonian captivity was sent: so they had done (<reference osisRef="Exod.32.4">Ex 32:4</reference>). After the return, and ever since, they have utterly forsaken idols.<div eID="gen15801" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15802" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wast called--</hi>as thine appropriate appellation (<reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>).<div eID="gen15802" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15803" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the womb--</hi>from the beginning of Israel's national existence (<reference osisRef="Isa.44.2">Is 44:2</reference>). <div eID="gen15803" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9250"/><div sID="gen15806" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9250"/>10. I sought by affliction to purify thee, but thou wast not as silver obtained by melting, but as dross [Gesenius]. Thy repentance is not complete: thou art not yet as refined silver. Rosenmuller explains, "not as silver," not with the intense heat needed to melt silver (it being harder to melt than gold), that is, not with the most extreme severity. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9256"/><div sID="gen15820" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9256"/><hi type="bold">16. not ... in secret--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.45.19">Is 45:19</reference>). Jehovah foretold Cyrus' advent, not with the studied ambiguity of heathen oracles, but plainly.<div eID="gen15820" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15821" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the time, &c.--</hi>From the moment that the purpose began to be accomplished in the raising up of Cyrus I was present.<div eID="gen15821" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15822" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sent me--</hi>The prophet here speaks, claiming attention to his announcement as to Cyrus, on the ground of his mission from God and His Spirit. But he speaks not in his own person so much as in that of Messiah, to whom alone in the fullest sense the words apply (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.1">Is 61:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.10.36">Joh 10:36</reference>). Plainly, <reference osisRef="Isa.49.1">Is 49:1</reference>, which is the continuation of the forty-eighth chapter, from <reference osisRef="Isa.48.16">Is 48:16</reference>, where the change of speaker from God (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.1">Is 48:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.48.12-Isa.48.15">12-15</reference>) begins, is the language of Messiah. <reference osisRef="Luke.4.1">Lu 4:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.14.18">14, 18</reference>, shows that the Spirit combined with the Father in sending the Son: therefore "His Spirit" is nominative to "sent," not accusative, following it. <div eID="gen15822" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 16. not ... in secret-- ( Is 45:19 ). Jehovah foretold Cyrus' advent, not with the studied ambiguity of heathen oracles, but plainly. from the time, &c.-- From the moment that the purpose began to be accomplished in the raising up of Cyrus I was present. sent me-- The prophet here speaks, claiming attention to his announcement as to Cyrus, on the ground of his mission from God and His Spirit. But he speaks not in his own person so much as in that of Messiah, to whom alone in the fullest sense the words apply ( Is 61:1 ; Joh 10:36 ). Plainly, Is 49:1 , which is the continuation of the forty-eighth chapter, from Is 48:16 , where the change of speaker from God ( Is 48:1 , 12-15 ) begins, is the language of Messiah. Lu 4:1 , 14, 18 , shows that the Spirit combined with the Father in sending the Son: therefore "His Spirit" is nominative to "sent," not accusative, following it.
entries.reader_content_plain: 16. not ... in secret-- ( Is 45:19 ). Jehovah foretold Cyrus' advent, not with the studied ambiguity of heathen oracles, but plainly. from the time, &c.-- From the moment that the purpose began to be accomplished in the raising up of Cyrus I was present. sent me-- The prophet here speaks, claiming attention to his announcement as to Cyrus, on the ground of his mission from God and His Spirit. But he speaks not in his own person so much as in that of Messiah, to whom alone in the fullest sense the words apply ( Is 61:1 ; Joh 10:36 ). Plainly, Is 49:1 , which is the continuation of the forty-eighth chapter, from Is 48:16 , where the change of speaker from God ( Is 48:1 , 12-15 ) begins, is the language of Messiah. Lu 4:1 , 14, 18 , shows that the Spirit combined with the Father in sending the Son: therefore "His Spirit" is nominative to "sent," not accusative, following it.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9261"/><div sID="gen15832" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9261"/>21. Ezra, in describing the return, makes no mention of God cleaving the rock for them in the desert [Kimchi]. The circumstances, therefore, of the deliverance from Egypt (<reference osisRef="Exod.17.6">Ex 17:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Num.20.11">Nu 20:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.78.15">Psa 78:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.105.41">105:41</reference>) and of that from Babylon, are blended together; the language, while more immediately referring to the latter deliverance, yet, as being blended with circumstances of the former not strictly applicable to the latter, cannot wholly refer to either, but to the mystic deliverance of man under Messiah, and literally to the final restoration of Israel. <div eID="gen15832" type="x-p"/>

Repeated (<reference osisRef="Isa.57.21">Is 57:21</reference>). All the blessings just mentioned (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.21">Is 48:21</reference>) belong only to the godly, not to the wicked. Israel shall first cast away its wicked unbelief before it shall inherit national prosperity (Zec 12:10-14; 13:1, 9; 14:3, 14, 20, 21). The sentiment holds good also as to all wicked men (Job 15:20-25, 31-34). <chapter eID="Isa.48"/>
